name: Battle of Navarino

phases.title: The Allied squadrons enter the bay
phases.text: The Ottoman and Egyptian fleet lay anchored in a horseshoe of three lines. The Allied ships came through the southern entrance in two lines, British and French to starboard and the Russians to port, slightly behind.

phases.title: The Allies anchor in the crescent
phases.text: The three British ships of the line anchored facing the Ottoman centre. The French took the side facing the Ottoman left wing, and the Russians the right end of the crescent. Allied captains had orders to fire only if attacked.

phases.title: Fighting breaks out at the entrance
phases.text: Dartmouth's boats were fired on when they tried to stop an Ottoman fireship, and the shooting spread along the line. Breslaw left the French formation to reinforce Albion and Azov in the centre.

phases.title: The centre fights at anchor
phases.text: Ships fired at very close range, with little room to manoeuvre. The French silenced the fort's battery. Asia concentrated her fire on Fahti Bahri, and Breslaw moved to the junction of the British and Russian lines.

phases.title: The Ottoman front line is despatched
phases.text: All three Ottoman ships of the line and most of the large frigates of the first line had been despatched. The small British and French vessels stopped the fireships, and only the first attack on Scipion got home.

phases.title: The smaller vessels are destroyed
phases.text: The Allied ships of the line, all still operational, fired on the second and third lines. Codrington tried twice to order a ceasefire, but his signals were hidden by smoke or ignored. Of 78 vessels, just eight stayed seaworthy.

note: The plan shows the bay as a schematic, not to scale. The accounts give the shape of the Ottoman line and which Allied squadron faced which part of it, but not exact anchorages. Where the Ottoman left and right wings lay on the page, and where the corvettes at the entrance stood, is placed by judgement. The Ottoman second and third lines are drawn as one block, and the Allied squadrons as one block each. Allied sources give the account of how the fighting began; Codrington's claim that the Ottomans began it is the account followed.
